I1_vs_I2.family_F_I: 8 tests: one McNemar (flip under I1 vs flip under I2, paired on post) per system; Holm
I1_vs_I2.flip_definition: verdict differs from the same system's ORIG verdict; only posts where ORIG, I1 and I2 are all answered

I3.construction: paraphrased by gemma2:9b (also evaluated); equivalence judged by qwen2.5:7b (also evaluated), two directions
I3.circularity_check: compare gemma2 (author of the paraphrases) and qwen2.5 (the judge) with the other systems on judge_equivalent vs judge_not_equivalent and human_valid vs human_invalid; descriptive only

direct_vs_evidence_ORIG.family_F_P: 3 tests per variant (one per model), x = evidence correct, y = direct correct; Holm

llm_vs_wordLR_ORIG.family_F_B: 6 tests per variant (each LLM condition vs word-LR), x = LLM correct, y = word-LR correct; Holm

human_validation.procedure: Ya/Tidak dropdown per item in human_validation.xlsx (hitl_sheet.py); a third 'Keputusan' column settles disagreements
human_validation.independence: not enforced: both raters' sheets are in the same workbook; whether raters saw each other's answers is not documented

oracle_validity.design: census + 20% sample, weights N_h/N, FPC on control
hatespeech and normal strata (400 items) never validated
oracle_validity.note: the unweighted 44.8% in validation.json mixes a census of ambiguous cases with a small control sample and does not describe R2

E1_residual_identity_terms.definition: E1 items: flagged = verdict 'violating'; identity term = any build_items.GROUP_TERMS token left in the E1 text; answered items only (refusals and unparseable excluded)
E1_residual_identity_terms.family_F_R: 8 Fisher tests (one per system) per variant; Holm
